name: Salmon
overview: Salmon was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Nahshon and the father of Boaz. His place in the genealogy of King David highlights his role in the Messianic lineage. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Salmon, also rendered Salma, means "little spark" in Hebrew. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but reflects a meaningful personal designation within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Salmon as the son of Nahshon and infers him as the father of Boaz. These familial ties place him within a significant ancestral line leading to King David.
scriptureSignificance: Salmon's significance lies in his position within the genealogy of King David, linking the leadership of Judah through Nahshon to Boaz and ultimately to the Messianic line. His mention in the book of Ruth underscores the continuity of God's covenant promises through faithful generations. This lineage exemplifies God's providential care in preserving the family line that would bring forth the Savior.
